items.title: What does the evidence establish about PayPal's languages?

queries.summary: The June 2020 case study documents Go in a NoSQL rewrite and build/test infrastructure. It is historical evidence, not a current company-wide language inventory.

source.label: Go case study with PayPal engineering leader

links.label: PayPal Taps Go to Modernize and Scale

caveats: This case study was published in 2020.

queries.summary: PayPal's squbs post documents Scala/Akka engineering; its 2024 Spark post discusses Scala compilation during migration.

source.label: PayPal engineering publications
caveats: These sources do not establish current company-wide adoption levels. The search did not establish increasing internal Rust adoption.

items.title: Does choosing a rare language earn explicit judging credit?

queries.summary: The official rules give equal weight to implementation, design, impact, innovation and presentation. They do not list programming-language rarity as a criterion.

source.label: PayPal AI Hackathon official rules
caveats: No measured relationship between language choice and award probability was available. The 30,000-participant figure is the user's scenario.

items.title: Which systems mechanisms support the proposed architecture?

queries.summary: Rust ownership addresses memory management. Wasmtime documents fuel-based deterministic interruption and its additional overhead. OTP supervisors can restart failed workers.

source.label: Official language and runtime documentation
caveats: These mechanisms do not by themselves guarantee valid payment authority, exactly-once effects or truthful product specifications.

queries.summary: The FoundationDB abstract describes deterministic simulation under faults. The Elle abstract describes transaction-history analysis for isolation violations.

source.label: Research metadata and abstracts retrieved through Undermind
caveats: Full paper text was unavailable in Undermind for this read. These techniques were not implemented or benchmarked in this assessment.
